items.title: Wikipedia's operator says a bad AI copyright ruling could threaten the open web
items.excerpt: The Wikimedia Foundation asked to file an amicus brief in New York Times v. OpenAI, arguing the court should treat AI training separately from chatbot outputs that reproduce copyrighted text, and warning that both sides' positions could harm open knowledge projects.

items.title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
items.excerpt: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic are implementing a new common setting that lets site owners opt out of having their content used for AI training, a shared standard arriving amid copyright litigation and transparency rules.

items.title: CMA opens investigation into Meta's commercial terms
items.excerpt: The UK CMA opened a Competition Act investigation into whether Meta's business terms, which would let it collect publishers' website content to develop its own products including AI features without a choice for those businesses, amount to unfair trading conditions.

history_match.title: Publishers want Brussels and London to stop Meta's new AI terms

items.title: Faster planning decisions as new rules and AI tackle delays
items.excerpt: The UK government announced new planning rules putting expert officers in charge of straightforward applications, alongside AI tools intended to cut delays in local planning decisions.

items.title: Thousands of "ghost students" use AI to steal millions in student loans, DOJ says
items.excerpt: The Justice Department says fraud rings used AI to enroll fake 'ghost students' and complete online coursework to collect federal student aid, and its crackdown may make FAFSA applications more demanding.

items.title: Democrats press OpenAI over safety researcher firings, security incidents
items.excerpt: Democratic lawmakers sent OpenAI a letter questioning its safety practices following the dismissal of three safety researchers and reported security incidents. (Off-list: congressional letter not covered by on-list outlets.)

history_match.title: Democrats warn tech firms of election security 'backsliding' ahead of midterms

items.title: Experts warn AI copyright changes could breach Australian constitution and spark huge compensation rights case
items.excerpt: Legal experts say proposed Australian copyright changes allowing AI training on creative works could amount to an acquisition of property under the constitution, exposing the government to compensation claims. (Off-list.)

items.title: "매번 동의" vs "고지 후 거부"…AI 시대 개인정보 활용 어떻게(종합)
items.excerpt: 행정안전부와 개인정보보호위원회가 국민 200명이 참여한 숙의 토론회를 열어, AI가 개인정보를 활용할 때마다 동의를 받을지 '사전 고지 후 거부권' 방식으로 바꿀지를 논의했다. 이해민 청와대 AI미래기획수석도 참석했다.

items.title: 정부 업무망서 인터넷 검색에 보고서 작성도…'온AI' 기능 확대
items.excerpt: 행정안전부가 공무원 업무망 AI 서비스 '온AI'에 최신 인터넷 정보 검색 기능을 넣고, 12월부터 한글 보고서 초안 작성을 지원하는 등 정부 내부 AI 활용을 확대한다.

items.title: 정부, AIDC 진입 장벽 낮춘다…하위법령 입법예고 앞두고 기준 완화 가닥
items.excerpt: 정부가 AI 데이터센터(AIDC) 특별법 하위법령을 이르면 이번 주 입법예고할 예정이며, 기존 데이터센터 일부를 AI용으로 전환해도 AIDC로 인정하는 등 인정 기준을 시행령 초안보다 완화하는 방향으로 조정했다.

items.title: EPIC Urges FCC to Protect Consumers from Unwanted "Political" Robocalls
items.excerpt: EPIC filed reply comments asking the FCC to deny a Club for Growth petition that would exempt political calls using artificial or prerecorded voices, including AI-generated voices, from TCPA consent rules. (Body date only: October 30, 2026.)

items.title: Judge says xAI must face NAACP lawsuit on data center pollution
items.excerpt: A federal judge denied xAI's motion to dismiss an NAACP Clean Air Act suit over gas turbines powering its AI data center operations in the Memphis area, letting the case proceed. (Off-list: court ruling not on on-list feeds.)

history_match.title: Judge rejects Trump's claim EPA can dismiss data center pollution lawsuits

items.title: Behind the Curtain: OpenAI's post-election power play
items.excerpt: Axios reports OpenAI plans a policy push in the lame-duck session starting Nov. 9, including proposals it frames as 'speed limits' and rebranding data centers as 'AI compute campuses'; claims attributed to OpenAI's Chris Lehane.

items.title: Websites pretending to be local news are boosting Democratic candidates
items.excerpt: NPR found ChatGPT citing a network of 37 sites of unknown origin, identified by security firm VisionHeight, that mimic local news while promoting candidates in competitive House races; the DCCC denied involvement. (Off-list: AI-chatbot election manipulation, no on-list equivalent.)

items.title: Prop 45 in California could be hiding a loophole for data centers
items.excerpt: The Verge reports critics say California's Proposition 45, on the Nov. 3 ballot, could carry a loophole benefiting data centers' energy projects; one critic says 'communities get cut out of the conversation.' Contested claims attributed to critics.

items.title: What Democrats Can Learn From New York's Data Center Moratorium
items.excerpt: With anti-data-center candidates on the ballot Tuesday, New York's data center moratorium shows the tensions governments face when acting on AI infrastructure.

history_match.title: Data centers face a sweeping new power regime

items.title: The Datacenter Backlash Goes Bipartisan: Next Week's Midterms and the 2028 Buildout
items.excerpt: SemiAnalysis argues local opposition to AI datacenters now spans both parties; 2027 capacity is largely locked in, but a prolonged Texas permit freeze is the biggest single risk to the 2028 buildout.

items.title: How Ireland plans to beat the data center backlash
items.excerpt: Ireland, Europe's tech capital and a 'canary in the coalmine' for the data center dilemma, is setting policy on how to accommodate AI-driven data center demand on a strained grid.

items.title: The Promise and Pitfalls of Nvidia's Venture in Kazakhstan
items.excerpt: Kazakhstan signed an investment agreement with Firebird for a Data Center Valley powered by 45,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs under newly announced US export licenses, with 10% of capacity reserved for domestic users; analysts flag power shortfalls.

history_match.title: Investment summit: German government strikes AI deal with Nvidia

items.title: Exclusive-Australian outback data centre pulls timeline after regulator stalls
items.excerpt: Startup Energy North, developer of one of Australia's biggest planned data centres, scrapped its target start date after a regulator said it needed longer than usual to set environmental parameters, a setback to Australia's bid to be a fast-track destination for AI investment (Reuters). (Off-list: datacenter siting regulation.)

items.title: Electrocutions, Intimidation and Wage Theft Haunt Europe's Data Center Workers
items.excerpt: An investigation finds migrant workers building US tech giants' AI data centers across Europe face injuries, squalid housing, unpaid wages and labor exploitation.

items.title: Is Half of China's AI Making Slop?
items.excerpt: ChinaTalk examines the claim that 55% of China's AI token usage goes to low-value content, and what Chinese usage data says about US-China AI competition.
